subject.title: fix: active-memory recall fails with billing rejections on subscription-only Claude CLI setups

question: Should subscription-backed embedded helpers use a generic provider capability and shared dispatch policy, or should core permanently expose the Claude-specific caller opt-in introduced here?
rationale: Both shapes can fix this recall bug, but the choice establishes a core runtime API, provider ownership boundary, and precedent for the other helper paths tracked in the related issue; repository policy does not permit automation to choose that permanent contract.

options.title: Adopt a generic backend capability
options.body: Move the Claude eligibility signal into provider-owned CLI backend metadata and let the embedded runner apply one generic dispatch rule shared by helper callers.

options.title: Approve the caller opt-in
options.body: Keep the new subscription-auth parameter and Claude-specific core eligibility after explicitly accepting the parallel dispatch seam and documenting its ownership.

options.title: Consolidate with broader helper routing
options.body: Pause this branch and implement the active-memory case through the canonical helper-dispatch work tracked at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/57326.

recommendation.title: Adopt a generic backend capability
recommendation.body: Move the Claude eligibility signal into provider-owned CLI backend metadata and let the embedded runner apply one generic dispatch rule shared by helper callers.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is the recent Claude CLI permission and runtime work in the central preparation path.
